mechanism_narrative: A continued recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT raises weekday foot traffic to shopping areas, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks because more commuters convert trips into retail visits.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -5.3 to -8.1 while TRANSIT stayed below baseline and RETAIL_REC stayed around -12
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior four weeks after WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while WORKPLACES remain weak, more time spent at home reduces discretionary shopping trips, causing RETAIL_REC to fall over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 5 points while WORKPLACES below 0 points for at least 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is positive in all four weeks while WORKPLACES turned negative at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 5 and WORKPLACES remaining below 0.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM reflects routine errand consolidation near neighborhood centers, which substitutes away from longer retail outings and keeps RETAIL_REC lower over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed positive at 11-15 points while RETAIL_REC remained negative
failure_condition: Reject if a further one-week increase in GROCERY_PHARM is followed by higher RETAIL_REC instead of lower RETAIL_REC.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT drops sharply from one week to the next, access friction for shopping districts rises and RETAIL_REC weakens over the following four weeks because fewer discretionary trips are completed.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by more than 2 points week-on-week from an already negative level
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -5.7 to -8.4 at t-0w while RETAIL_REC remained near -12
failure_condition: Reject if a week-on-week TRANSIT decline larger than 2 points is followed by no further deterioration in RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward move in PARKS draws weekend leisure demand away from malls and dining districts, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -37.1 to -24.0 while RETAIL_REC did not improve
failure_condition: Reject if continued PARKS recovery is followed by a higher mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM stays positive while PARKS also rebounds, household trip chains become locally concentrated and discretionary retail visits are crowded out, lowering RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM above 10 points and PARKS above -30 points
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed above 10 and PARKS rose to -24.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if the joint condition of high GROCERY_PHARM and improving PARKS is followed by any increase in RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days.

mechanism_narrative: During a demand-recovery regime, the combination of improving WORKPLACES and TRANSIT transmits into retail visits with a lag, so RETAIL_REC turns higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved back toward zero before dropping at t-0w; TRANSIT remained less negative than at t-3w
failure_condition: Reject if retail activity does not improve over 28 days after a period in which WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both trend upward.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL rises above its recent range while TRANSIT stays depressed, mobility is shifting toward stay-at-home behavior and retail visits weaken over the next one week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL above 8 points and TRANSIT below -7 points
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL was 7.6 at t-0w and TRANSIT was -8.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: Reject if RETAIL_REC does not fall within 7 days after RESIDENTIAL exceeds 8 while TRANSIT remains below -7.
